outcome: Go-live document review records the reviewer's verdict on the exact version
acceptance_criteria: On the live-shaped work read (`4601`, `tasks: []`) the go-live page shows no review control and no error — verify: `cd frontend && npx playwright test e2e/go-live-review.spec.ts` (Next 4990, mock 4991) asserts the heading "Review the go-live document" is absent.

`readReviewSubject` returns `null` for the real 1.25.0 work read and for the go-live-signoff and go-live-replies reads; no code path takes `version_id` from user input, a URL parameter, or `document-versions` — verify: unit test on the function; `grep -rn "version_id" frontend/src/features/go-live/GoLiveReviewActions.tsx` shows it only as a prop.
With a subject (`4602`), the form shows "Version 5120", the three verdicts unselected, and the button is off — verify: component test and e2e screenshot at 1440 and 390 px.
A subject that is present but `can_decide` is false (`4603`) draws nothing — verify: component test.
Only the verdicts in the subject's `verdicts[]` are offered; a subject with `[approve, return]` offers no reject — verify: component test.

Approve sends exactly `{kind:"document", expected_revision:7, case_revision:12, version_id:5120, verdict:"approve", note:""}` with the work read's revisions and no other key — verify: unit test on the request body.
Return and reject with a blank note do not send and say a reason is required; with text they send the note unchanged — verify: component test counts calls.

After a 200 the form shows "Review recorded: Approved" and `review_id` when present, the work is refetched once, and the page shows the refetched `state`; with `review_id: null` it shows the result without an id — verify: e2e with `4604`; unit test on null.
A double click on "Record my review" sends exactly one POST — verify: unit test with a slow mock counts calls.

A 409 (`4605`) shows "This changed while you were working. We reloaded it. Check it and try again.", re-reads the work, keeps the typed note, and the next press sends the new revisions — verify: e2e compares revision values in the two POST bodies.
A 422 `STALE_VERSION` (`4606`) shows the server's text inline and records nothing — verify: component test.

Wrong user or wrong tenant: a 404 on the work read (`4607`) and a 403 on the POST both show exactly "This record is unavailable." with no difference between them and no form — verify: e2e and mapper unit test.

A 403 `csrf_failed` refreshes the session once and says "Press the button again"; no second POST is sent automatically. A lost response says "Check the record before trying again" after re-reading the work, with no automatic retry — verify: unit tests count calls.
The control is not drawn for a work item on any line other than `delivery-go-live/v1` — verify: unit test with another `line`.
Nothing on this page sends, publishes or previews the document to the client; no "send" control exists — verify: e2e asserts the text and controls list.
No Tola, agent step or "ask the agent" wording appears (D-182) — verify: `grep -rni "tola" frontend/src/features/go-live/GoLiveReviewActions.tsx` returns nothing.

`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` contains no file under `frontend/src/features/workspace/`, `frontend/src/features/work-item/`, none of F-114's or F-114B's files other than the one registration line, and none of `delivery/checks.sh`, `delivery/config.json`, `delivery/merge-policy.json` — verify: command output.
build.md lists the held write, the test-only seam, the one-line `server.mjs` change, and each board part hidden — verify: file content.

risk.rationale: High. A document approval is a recorded independent decision that lets the go-live document go to the client, and it is hard to undo. The server enforces who may review and independence (`apps/core/factory_api` reviews, `backend-answers.md` C-5 and C-29 for the `reviews` pattern), so auth and external-messaging are surfaces along with ui and api. Product acceptance is required because the reviewer flow and its wording are new and client-visible. The `version_id` source for a non-PM reviewer is the one open detail, and the spec writer settles it from the work read.
